checks.rule: Urban title-plan basis commonly uses 1:1250 mapping; rural commonly 1:2500; mountain/moorland may use 1:10000.
At 1:1250, mapped line width roughly represents 0.3 m on the ground.
At 1:2500, mapped line width roughly represents 0.6 m on the ground.
Scaled map measurements may not exactly match ground measurements because mapping has specified accuracy tolerances.
1:1250 relative accuracy has <±0.5 m relative error and <±0.9 m at 95% confidence for the stated test distance.
1:2500 resurvey/reformed relative accuracy has <±1.0 m relative error and <±1.9 m at 95% confidence.
1:1250 absolute accuracy RMSE is <±0.5 m with <±0.8 m at 95% confidence.
1:2500 resurvey/reformed absolute accuracy RMSE is <±1.1 m with <±1.9 m at 95% confidence.
Do not promote a parcel boundary coordinate as survey-grade merely because it was digitised from a title-plan line.
Do not treat enlargement of mapping as an accuracy improvement; original survey specification remains controlling.
Do not infer a sub-metre parcel edge from line-centre scaling when the source mapping tolerance is larger.
Keep horizontal boundary uncertainty separate from vertical elevation uncertainty in any height-difference result.
